name: aitp-console
//aitp: SDK floors that are load-bearing for THIS app, each with its consequence if violated -- same convention, and the same position, as `aitp-control-plane/package.json`'s `//aitp`: the rationale for a non-obvious version floor must live next to it or it is lost. This console is a *verifier*, never an issuer: the only SDK symbol imported anywhere here is `verifyManifestJson` (`src/lib/api/verify-manifest.ts:1`). Since CP1.1 the CP signs no revocation list, so the console verifies none (`verifyRevocationList` was dropped with the well-known route); revocation codes still reach it only inside playground run events. A verifier does not choose what arrives on the wire, which is why this comment and CP's can reach different conclusions about the same release. `0.24.0` (current, BEHAVIOURAL for a verifier): still `aitp/0.3` Manifests, no wire-version change. The breaking items are the Rust stable/experimental split (RS-RC4) and the RS-RC7b API rework (typed errors, immutable `Verified*` results, one revocation model, variable-length signatures). In the Node SDK, renewal, Session Trust Bundles and multi-hop delegation (`buildRenewalRequest`, `processRenewalRequest`, `SessionBundleBuilder`, `verifySessionBundle`, `verifyDelegationMultihop`) leave the published package. The console uses none of them: `verifyManifestJson`, plus the test-only `AitpAgent.generate` / `buildManifest` / `signRevocationList` / `verifyRevocationList`, keep their signatures and documented code sets in the stable `index.d.ts`, and the SDK pins in `src/test/sdk-verification.integration.test.ts` pass untouched. `verify_manifest` now checks proof of possession before the signature (RFC-AITP-0003 §5), so a Manifest that fails BOTH checks is `pop_failed` where it was `signature_invalid`, and `pop_failed` no longer implies a verified signature. The console used to render it as 'REJECTED · signature verified · proof-of-possession failed', which would now be an overclaim on a forged Manifest. It now renders red as 'proof-of-possession failed · signature not assessed' (`MANIFEST_PRE_SIGNATURE_REJECTION_DETAIL` in `src/lib/verification-display.ts`, reused by the run-timeline card). `identity_hint_malformed` is still checked after the signature and keeps the 'signature verified' row. `src/test/sdk-verification.integration.test.ts` pins `pop_failed` for a both-tampered Manifest and `signature_invalid` for a signature-only tamper. The SDK requires Node >= 20 (`engines.node`); the console requires >= 22.13. It also publishes linux musl binaries, so the lockfile now carries six platform packages; `check-aitp-lock.mjs` still requires the four gnu/darwin ones. `0.20.0`-`0.23.0` (ROUTINE for a verifier): still `aitp/0.3` Manifests; `verifyManifestJson`'s signature and code set are unchanged, and the whole suite, including the SDK pins in `src/test/sdk-verification.integration.test.ts` (`unknown_field`, `malformed`, the `version_unknown` CUTOVER, the externally minted manifests), passes untouched. Every breaking item is issuer- or handshake-side and none reaches the console: revocation is `fail_closed` by default in `verifyTct` / `verifyDelegation` / session completion (0.20; the console calls none), `buildManifest` gains `revocationListUri` (0.20) and `acceptedIdentityTypes` (0.22; it defaults to the agent's own type, so binding-built Manifests now carry `accepted_identity_types`, which verifies since `0.12.0`), handshake failures carry `.code` (0.22), PoP helpers are new (0.21), schema `$id`s moved off `aitp.dev` (0.20; the console resolves no schema), and `IdentityDescriptor` gains optional `svid_type` / `x5c` (0.22). `0.23.0` itself is CLI-only. `0.19.0` (ROUTINE for a verifier): still `aitp/0.3`, no wire change (`aitp-rs/docs/upgrading-0.19.md`). Its break (#279) is binding-side signing and deny-list input: `signEnvelope` `messageId` and `SessionBundleBuilder.sessionId` must be lowercase UUID v4, and each `revokedJtis` entry is normalized (non-UUID throws). The console calls none of them (only `verifyManifestJson` / `verifyRevocationList`, neither takes `revokedJtis`). `0.18.0` (ROUTINE for a verifier): still `aitp/0.3`, no wire change (`aitp-rs/docs/upgrading-0.18.md`). Its breaking items do not reach this console: signing now refuses a non-lowercase or non-v4 `jti` (the console never signs; verify was already strict, so such a `jti` on the wire is still `malformed`, amber), and an unknown snapshot version is `REVOCATION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID` only in the Rust adapter and `RevocationCache`. The Node `verifyRevocationList` cause stays `version_unknown` (amber, CUTOVER test unchanged). `0.17.0` (PROTOCOL-LOAD-BEARING): strict `aitp/0.2` -> `aitp/0.3` cutover for Manifests and revocation snapshots. `verify_manifest` and `verify_revocation_list` check version before expiry and signature, so a `0.12`-`0.16` console reading a `0.17` CP (or the reverse) gets `version_unknown` on every artifact. That renders amber ('signature not assessed'), never red, and `src/test/sdk-verification.integration.test.ts` pins it (CUTOVER). The console therefore deploys together with `aitp-control-plane` (CP first, console minutes after), never alone. Signatures of `buildManifest` / `signRevocationList` / `verifyManifestJson` / `verifyRevocationList` are unchanged; `verifyEnvelope` / `signEnvelope` are new and deliberately not adopted (no envelopes reach the console). `0.15.0` (BEHAVIOURAL): both Node entry points now run the hardened wire parser before verifying (`wire::manifest` / `wire::revocation_snapshot`, `bindings/aitp-node/src/lib.rs:79-95`). A member outside the schema is now `unknown_field` (was `malformed` via serde `deny_unknown_fields` on `0.10.0`-`0.14.x`); a duplicate key is `malformed`; a revocation `entries[].jti` that is not UUID v4 is `malformed`. All three are pre-signature and classified amber at `src/lib/verification-display.ts` (`MANIFEST_UNASSESSED_CODES`, `REVOCATION_UNASSESSED_CODES`). Without that classification `unknown_field` falls through to a red 'VERIFICATION FAILED' -- an overclaim. `0.12.0` (historical floor, still true): fixes two false REJECTIONS only a verifier can hit. (1) `accepted_signature_algorithms` was not a member of `Manifest` until `0.12.0`, so on `0.10.0` an AUTHENTIC manifest carrying that spec-legal member threw `malformed` -- a false amber. (2) `Manifest::extensions` dropped a wire-present `"extensions":{}` from the signing input until fix `b78e608` made it `Option<ExtensionsMap>`, so on `0.10.0` such a manifest threw `signature_invalid` -- a RED badge on an authentic artifact. Evidence: `src/test/fixtures/minted-manifests.ts` (externally minted by `aitp-verifier-py`, re-minted for `aitp/0.3`). CP, an issuer building through `ManifestOpts`, cannot emit either shape, which is why CP did not treat `0.12.0` as load-bearing. `0.7.0` (historical floor): the first release where a `verifyManifestJson` failure carries a typed `.code`; `verify-manifest.ts` branches on `typeof code === 'string'`, and below this floor every failure would be misclassified as `sdk_unavailable`. READING RELEASE BOUNDARIES: `aitp-rs/CHANGELOG.md` carries proper `## [X.Y.Z] — date` release headers from `0.12.0` through `0.22.0` (and `0.23.0` / `0.24.0`, though at tag `aitp-v0.23.0` its entries still sat under `## [Unreleased]`; read the headers on `main` or a later tag), and there are no `docs/upgrading-0.N.md` guides after `0.19` (read the CHANGELOG instead); git tags `aitp-vX.Y.Z` and npm agree from `aitp-v0.11.0` on (the old `aitp-v0.10.0` tag is NOT npm 0.10.0; that tree is `c7a7159`). Do not gate a bump on an `index.d.ts` diff: the behavioural changes above were invisible to it. RANGE CHOICE `^0.24.0`: on a 0.x range npm's caret pins the MINOR, so only `0.24.x` patches float and `0.25.0` needs a deliberate edit. LOCKFILE: npm 11 updating the pin in place pruned three of the four platform packages (incl. `linux-x64-gnu`, the one Vercel runs); drop the `aitp` + `@agentidentitytrustprotocol/*` lock entries and reinstall, then check all four are present with `libc` on the linux ones. BUMP AUTOMATION: `.github/workflows/bump-aitp.yml` (shared `aitp-ci` `bump-consume.yml@v1`, same as CP) opens a `deps/aitp-<version>` PR on the `aitp-released` dispatch, a weekly schedule, or by hand. It re-locks with `npm install --package-lock-only`, which keeps all four platform packages, and CI's `scripts/check-aitp-lock.mjs` fails any lockfile that drops one. On 0.x every minor counts as breaking, so it does NOT arm auto-merge: read `docs/upgrading-0.N.md` (or the CHANGELOG where none exists), add a note above, merge, then deploy prod by hand. Dependabot ignores the SDK so the two never race. Before this the caret drifted five minors (`0.12` -> `0.17`) unnoticed.
